rows.new_text: Copies waiting for your decision. Compare each copy's Calmar, CAGR and drawdown with the original before you approve; approving creates a new undeployed symphony and trades nothing.
The guard effect is how the bot's exits compare with holding every symphony through, over the window you pick. Above zero the exits did better than holding; below zero holding would have done better.
Windows: 30d to 1Y are calendar days counted back from the session shown. YTD starts on 1 January; All time uses every recorded day.
Bot: the return with the bot's exits applied. While live trading is off it is a simulation that places no order, and the headline then says Simulated.
If held: what the same symphonies would have returned with no exit, held as Composer runs them.
Shadow history: the bot's own daily record of both paths, kept for the last {shadow_retention_days} days.
Account · all-time: Composer's own total return for the whole account since it was opened; it does not change with the window.

rows.term: All symphonies at their latest values, before trading costs
rows.new_text: At their latest values: each symphony is weighted by its current value; before trading costs: no cost of trading is taken off.

rows.term: the info mark on the first row
rows.new_text: The first row's Held figure is for the whole account, uninvested cash included; a card's Held figure leaves cash out.
α: the bot's edge over holding on that row. Positive is good for the bot: a higher return, a shallower fall or calmer swings.
Bars: the highlighted bar and label mark the better side on that row.
Value-weighted floor: Composer's account totals could not be read, so the row weights each symphony by its value instead.
Stale account data: Composer's account totals could not be refreshed, so the row uses the last totals read, from the time shown.
Cumulative · lifetime: Composer's Total return since each symphony was invested, which counts deposits and withdrawals; it is not a time-weighted return.
Max DD: maximum drawdown, the largest fall from a high to a later low in the window, shown as a size. The row waits until the window holds enough trading days for a stable figure.
Ann. vol: annualized volatility, how widely daily returns swing, scaled to a year; lower is calmer.
Lifetime Max DD · since inception: the deepest fall of your symphonies held through, from Composer's records since each was invested, weighted by value.
Tracked counts every symphony the bot watches. Armed counts those with a stop set and waiting, and Triggered counts those the bot has exited.
Exit: one time the bot sold a symphony out. Saved or lost: the symphony's value times the gap between its exit return and its held return, added over the exits.
Snapshot-time basis: each exit valued at the bot's afternoon check of that day.
Gross of trading costs: before any cost of trading the exit.

Net of trading costs: after taking {friction_pct} percentage points off every exit, the cost the autotune assumes for each exit. With many exits the net result sits well below the gross one: fewer dollars saved, or more lost.
Realized (marks basis): each exit valued at its day's end-of-day prices instead of the afternoon check; the count says how many exits have those prices.
N locked: how many tuning variables are locked across your symphonies; the weekly autotune leaves those alone.

rows.term: a session date after the heading
rows.new_text: A date after the heading: the figures below belong to that session, not today.
Trailing stop: the exit fired because the symphony fell further below its peak than its volatility-scaled stop allows.
Take-profit: the exit fired to keep a gain the Monte Carlo check judged likely to fade.

VWAP breakdown: the exit fired after the symphony had gained enough to arm this check, its holdings then traded below their volume-weighted average price, and its return stayed under the session high for several checks in a row.

VWAP bleed: the exit fired after the symphony's own return stayed at or below a volatility-scaled loss line for several checks in a row; despite the name, this check does not look at the volume-weighted average price.
Armed: the trailing stop is set and following the symphony's peak.
TP-armed: the take-profit is set and waiting for its confirmation.
Para-armed: the symphony rose fast enough that its stop has been pulled in closer.

rows.term: Exit beat holding, Exit trailed holding
rows.new_text: Exit beat or trailed holding: the exit's return minus the symphony's held return.
vs held now: compared with the held return at this minute, so the figure moves while the market is open. At close: compared at the session's close.
Lifetime Max DD: this symphony's deepest fall since it was invested, from Composer's records, held through.

rows.term: the first ledger column, a date or Today with α
rows.new_text: The first column is the session's return; its α is the bot's edge over holding for that session.
Bot · frozen: after an exit the Bot figure stays at the exit's return while If held keeps moving.
If held · live: the held return, still moving with the market after the exit.
Cum: return since the symphony was invested, from Composer; the Bot side adds the exits' effect over the shadow history.
Max DD on a card: each side's deepest fall over the shadow history; a positive α means the bot's fall was shallower.

The ring: the Monte Carlo reading, the share of similar past market days on which this symphony's holdings did better than they are doing now. A low reading means today is unusually strong; a dash means no reading.
Sparkline: the session's return; a TP, VWAP or Stop badge marks the minute of an exit.
Symphonies the bot is watching with no stop armed. A symphony moves up to Active when a stop arms or the bot exits it.
CVaR: expected shortfall, the average of the outcomes in the worst tail the heading names.
stderr: the standard error, how far the figure could be off by chance alone.
Tail obs: how many outcomes fell in that tail; a small count means a rough figure.
Lower bound: the method tends to understate how bad the tail is, so the real figure is likely worse.
Atlas cache: the age of the weekly saved copy of the community strategy catalog the builders read.
Capital: the money assigned to the sleeve.
Ledger cash: the sleeve's uninvested cash by its own books.
Realized: gains or losses already closed out; n/a means the books could not be read.
Rule line: the rule's mode in brackets, then how often it fired today and over its life, and what those fires realized.

rows.term: Return, Live return, frozen at exit, at close, real-time
rows.new_text: Return: the symphony's return in the session; frozen at exit after an exit, at close once the market has closed, real-time while it is open.
Stop level: the return at which the bot exits; breakeven lock means the stop has been raised to protect the gain, vol-scaled means it follows the symphony's volatility.
Peak (HWM): the highest return the symphony itself reached in the session; until an exit, the stop trails this peak, and after an exit the figure keeps following the held return.
Exit α: the exit's return minus the held return, for this symphony.
Bot (booked): the bot's path; it moves with the symphony until an exit and then stays at the exit's return.
Breakeven lock: once the gain is large enough, the stop is raised so that the exit cannot fall below breakeven.
VWAP: the day's volume-weighted average price.
MC probability: the share of similar past market days on which this symphony's holdings did better than they are doing now; lower means today is unusually strong.
Parabolic velocity: how fast the return is climbing; past the threshold, the stop is pulled in closer.
Active · floor: the breakeven lock has fired and the stop cannot go below the floor shown.
VWAP defense: whether the symphony's holdings trade above or below their volume-weighted average price, and by how much; below it after a gain is what the VWAP breakdown exit watches for.
locked: the weekly autotune may not change this variable.
Windows: calendar days counted back from the session shown; YTD starts on 1 January and 5Y covers five years.
If held: the same symphonies held with no exit. Bot (shadow): the bot's shadow record, the return with its exits applied; while live trading is off it is a simulation that places no order.
Sharpe: return per unit of overall volatility; higher is better.
Sortino: return per unit of downside volatility only; higher is better.
Max DD reduction: how much shallower the bot's deepest fall was than holding's, in percentage points.
Max DD: the largest fall from a high to a later low over the window, shown as a size.
Calmar: yearly return divided by the deepest fall; higher is better.
Annualized volatility: how widely daily returns swing, scaled to a year.
Volatility reduction: how much calmer the bot's returns were than holding's, in percentage points.
Total return: the whole window's return, compounded.
Annualized return (CAGR): the yearly rate that compounds to the total return.
Up days: the share of days with a gain.
Sample: which daily series was checked, Replay or Shadow, as the note above says.
ρ: lag-1 autocorrelation, how much one day's return tends to carry into the next.
CI: the confidence range that ρ likely sits in.
Daily Sharpe: the average daily return divided by its volatility, not annualized.
N: how many daily returns the sample holds.
Sufficient met: even at the low end of its range, the day-to-day carry beats the daily Sharpe ratio, which is enough to justify the stop on average.
Sufficient likely: the carry beats the daily Sharpe ratio at its central estimate, but its range overlaps it.
Not met: this sample does not show enough carry; that is not proof the stop is wrong, and it says nothing about drawdown protection.
Negative edge: the daily Sharpe ratio is zero or below, so no carry can justify the stop on return grounds.
Insufficient data: too few days to judge either way.
Autotune: the weekly search for better stop settings; its last run leaves the replay series this table reads.
Retained: the days of exit history still kept; a count covers only those days.
Est. annual trading-cost drag: an estimate of the yearly return lost to trading costs, at {friction_pct} percentage points per exit times the exits per year.
Windows: calendar days counted back from the session shown; YTD starts on 1 January and 5Y covers five years.
Exit alpha: an exit's return minus its held return, in pts, which are percentage points.

rows.term: the time in the exit-alpha note
rows.new_text: The time in the note: when the bot freezes each exit's result for the day's record, the same afternoon check the dashboard calls snapshot-time.
Dollar result: the dollars the exits saved or lost against holding, on the same snapshot basis as the dashboard.
Win rate: the share of exits whose exit alpha was above zero.
Wins: exits whose exit alpha was above zero. Avg per exit: the reason's sum of exit alpha divided by its number of exits.
Each exit of the day in the heading: when it fired, the symphony, the rule, and in Detail its exit alpha.
Composer: the key and secret the bot reads your symphonies and sends sell orders with, and your account ids.
Alpaca · price data: the keys the bot reads market prices with.
Discord + Anthropic: the webhook for alerts and the key the advisor uses.

rows.term: uses globals, N overrides, lock, override
rows.new_text: uses globals: no value set for this symphony. N overrides: values set for this symphony. lock: stop the autotune changing a value. override: a value that replaces the global one.
No longer held: Composer no longer reports this symphony and the engine writes it no rows; it returns here by itself if its rows resume.
Synthetic post-mortem: a daily exit record that was generated or seeded rather than captured live. Re-syncs account totals: reads the account totals from Composer again.
Dry-run (global off): the server's live switch is off, so nothing trades live. Live: this symphony sends real sell orders. Dry-run: this symphony is watched but sends no orders.
Clear: the check passed. Watch: worth a look, not a failure. Breach: the check failed.

rows.term: the mode pill, Dry run or Live
rows.new_text: Dry run: global live execution is off, so the bot sends no real orders. Live: global live execution is on; a symphony trades live only when its own live switch is on too.

states.Dry run: Dry run: global live execution is off, so the bot sends no real orders.
states.Live: Live: global live execution is on; a symphony trades live only when its own live switch is on too.

rows.new_text: Live: the market is open and the engine is checking stops every minute. Closed: the market is closed. Rebalance pause: the scheduled pause before the close; stops resume at the close. Opening: the session's first cycle is running. Stale: no recent engine cycle, so positions may not be guarded. Not updating: the page has not received data for a while. Degraded: the server reports a problem, named in the tooltip. Connection Lost: the last refresh failed, and the values shown are from the last data received. Each state carries only its own sentence.

states.Live: Live: the market is open and the engine is checking stops every minute.
states.Rebalance pause: Rebalance pause: the scheduled pause before the close; stops resume at the close.
states.Opening: Opening: the session's first cycle is running.
states.Stale: Stale: no recent engine cycle, so positions may not be guarded.
states.Not updating: Not updating: the page has not received data for a while.
states.Degraded: Degraded: the server reports a problem, named in the tooltip.
states.Connection Lost: Connection Lost: the last refresh failed, and the values shown are from the last data received.

rows.new_text: Account: the Composer account the dashboard shows figures for; choosing another reloads the dashboard for it. The short code is the start of the account's id.
Force run now: asks the server for an engine run; the server declines and answers that runs come only from the scheduler, so pressing it starts nothing.

Emergency Liquidate: after you choose an account and type LIQUIDATE, asks Composer to sell every symphony in that whole account to cash. While global live execution is off it only logs and sends the alert, and sells nothing.

rows.term: the dot beside a tab name
rows.new_text: Tab dots: green marks low risk; amber marks a tab to read with more care: higher overfitting risk, a real Composer write, or explanations only.
Model not known: the page has no Claude model name to show, because the lookup has not run yet, failed, or found no model of that family.
OOS: out of sample, recent history the tuning never saw, kept back to check that a result is not fitted to noise.
Confidence: the model's own rating of a suggestion, not a statistical test.

rows.term: allowlist, risk direction, oos frozen eval, locked vars
rows.new_text: Gates: allowlist checks the setting is one the advisor may suggest; risk direction checks that the direction the model claims for its change, looser or tighter, matches the direction the engine works out; oos frozen eval checks the change holds up on held-back history; locked vars checks the setting is not locked.

rows.term: Fallback OOS (on an empty run, built by static/ai_advisor.js)
rows.new_text: Fallback OOS: the same held-back score for the settings the symphony had before the latest autotune.

rows.term: Runs without adopting a tuned config
rows.new_text: Runs without adopting a tuned config: how many runs in a row kept the old settings.
CRRA-EU score: the autotune's score for a set of settings, an average outcome in which losses weigh more than gains of the same size; higher is better.
Sel t-stat: how clearly the winning settings stand out after correcting for how many settings were tried; higher is stronger.
Fallback: the new settings failed the check on held-back data, so the symphony keeps the settings it had before the run.
Frozen-eval: a final score of the run's best settings on held-back data, under the same objective; not evaluated means the run recorded no such score.
N/A: the run recorded no figure for that column.
risk-on: conditions favor taking risk. risk-off: they favor caution. neutral: no lean either way. limited-inputs: too few lenses had data for a read.

Lenses: technicals reads price trends and breadth, sentiment reads news tone, derivatives reads volatility measures, macro reads rates, inflation and jobs data, and fundamentals reads company filings.

Numeric verification: each number the read lists as a cited figure is checked against lens data fetched after the read; verified means it matched, and unverifiable means there was nothing to check it against, not that it is wrong. Numbers that appear only in the prose are not checked.

rows.term: THEORY spec, backtest-selection degrees of freedom
rows.new_text: THEORY spec: the frozen set of objective settings every tuning run shares, such as its risk aversion and utility family. Backtest-selection degrees of freedom: choices made by looking at backtest results, each of which adds overfitting risk.
Asset Swap and Logic Change: the weekly searches for a better ticker or rule in each symphony.

rows.term: Clear, Watch, Breach, Adopt candidate, Keep incumbent
rows.new_text: Clear: the check passed. Watch: worth a look, not a failure. Breach: the check failed. Adopt candidate: a candidate passed the gate and beat the current symphony. Keep incumbent: no candidate beat the current symphony.
Correlation: a number from minus 1 to 1 for how closely two return series move together; 1 is in lockstep and 0 is unrelated.
Stored no pairs: the run analysed the symphonies but saved no pair figures, so there is nothing to draw until a newer run saves them.

rows.term: the legend bands and thin markers
rows.new_text: Fill and markers: the fill deepens as the correlation gets stronger; a thin marker means the pair shares few days, so its figure is rough.
Deposit-adjusted: the series Composer names deposit-adjusted, which the recommender uses instead of the raw account value series.
Analysed: symphonies with a usable daily series, of all live symphonies.
History: the shortest and longest daily series, in days.
Pairs screened: pairs whose correlation reached the screen, of all pairs compared.
Blocked: screened pairs that did not become a recommendation, counted by the check that stopped them.
Run recommender: runs the nightly analysis now; it takes a minute or two and is refused while the market is open.
kept: the symphony of the pair that stays; the one before the arrow is the one suggested for retirement.
Composite gap: how far the kept symphony's combined return and risk score is ahead of the flagged one's.
Uncertainty gate: passes only if the correlation is still at or above the screen at the low end of its confidence range, so a high reading from a short history does not count.
Structural-redundancy gate: passes only if the two still move together on the worst {stress_fraction_pct} percent of days, when diversification matters most.
Approve retirement: records your decision and shows a wind-down checklist; it sells nothing and changes nothing in Composer.
Run tenure review: runs the review now instead of waiting for the nightly run; it is refused while the market is open.
trigger: whether the run was the nightly one or one you started. threshold in effect: the trading days a symphony needs before it gets a verdict.
keep: no evidence against it.
watch: it trails its own backtest by more than {watch_trail_pp} percentage points of total return, or the portfolio would have a higher return and no deeper drawdown without it.
retire-candidate: it duplicates another live symphony and scores lower, as under Correlated pairs.
no verdict: there is not yet enough evidence to judge.
basis: which series the figures use, Composer's realized one or the bot's shadow history. missing: evidence items that could not be computed, with the reason.

rows.term: not applicable, paired with, normalized across N symphonies
rows.new_text: not applicable: the item does not apply to this symphony, for the reason shown. paired with: the live symphony this one is compared against. normalized across N symphonies: the score is ranked among that many symphonies.
Performance: the symphony's realized return and risk over its tenure.
Composite score: its return and risk score ranked against the other live symphonies.
Redundancy: its return correlation with the other live symphonies.
Backtest: Composer's backtest of its current rules, against what it really earned.
Marginal contribution: the portfolio of eligible symphonies with and without it.
Long VIX hedge: its long-volatility holdings beside the rest of the portfolio, shown for context and not used in the verdict.

The gate: a candidate must beat the current symphony on history held back from the test, beat SPY over the same period, pass the overfitting check, and survive a correction for how many candidates were tested.
Baseline: the symphony as it is. Variant: the symphony with the change.
PBO: probability of backtest overfitting, the chance the best-looking candidate looked best by luck; a high PBO vetoes the candidate.
Model and context: which model reasoned and which evidence it was given.
FDR/Yekutieli correction: raises the bar each candidate must clear as more candidates are tested, so one lucky result among many tries is not taken for skill.
Sound-but-unprovable: passed every check, which still does not prove it will work live.

rows.term: Reduce drawdown, Lift risk-adjusted return, Reduce turnover
rows.new_text: Objectives: reduce drawdown aims for shallower falls, lift risk-adjusted return aims for more return per unit of risk, and reduce turnover aims for fewer trades.
Baseline: the symphony as it is. Variant: the symphony with the change. Ann. return: yearly return.
Adjusted threshold α: the p-value bar after the correction for how many candidates were tested. p: the candidate's p-value, which must be under the bar to pass.
Community: strategies from the Atlas library, a public catalog of Composer strategies, ranked for your goal.
FDR/Yekutieli correction: raises the bar each candidate must clear as more candidates are tested, so one lucky result among many tries is not taken for skill.

rows.term: Diversify, Cut drawdown, Lift risk-adjusted return
rows.new_text: Objectives: diversify favors strategies that share few holdings with yours, cut drawdown favors shallow falls, and lift risk-adjusted return favors a higher Sharpe ratio.
Universe (tickers): the tickers the designed strategies may use; leave it empty to allow every tradeable US-listed stock and fund.
PBO: probability of backtest overfitting, the chance the best-looking candidate looked best by luck; a high PBO vetoes the candidate.
Live Baseline: the same figures for your live symphony over the same days as the candidate's backtest.
Incubating: paper-tracked forward before it is shown as a recommendation. Promoted: its forward results held up. Failed: they did not, or its fall went too deep. Expired: tracking stopped.

Incumbent: your current symphony. Frontrunner overlay: a rule placed ahead of the symphony's own logic that switches into VIX-linked funds when its conditions are met, for example a watched ticker's RSI rising above a set level.
Same title: several cards can copy the same symphony; they differ in their overlay and figures, which View the added overlay shows.
Strategy Builder (retrofit): a from-scratch Strategy Builder design offered for this symphony; it does not contain the incumbent's logic.
Calmar: yearly return divided by the deepest fall; higher is better. CAGR: the yearly growth rate. Max DD: the deepest fall from a high to a later low.
Node count change: how many more or fewer steps the copy's rule tree has than the original; fewer is simpler.
